Mosaic

A study environment in English and French that transcribes lectures on the device, produces structured notes, and then asks the learner to explain, retrieve and apply the material through a sequence of tasks modelled on the Feynman technique.

Visit the site ↗How to useEngineering record

Engineering recordFor technical reviewers

Designed and shipped a bilingual learning platform: data model with row-level security, on-device transcription, AI routes with structural validation, spaced repetition and the test suite. The guiding rule was that a learner’s files stay on the device.

A learner imports a lecture video. Whisper, compiled to WebAssembly, transcribes it in a worker on the device; only the transcript and a few still frames go to the notes route, which asks Claude for a draft. Visual specifications returned by the model are validated for structure and meaning before they play, and sent back once for repair if they fail. Cards made from the note are scheduled with FSRS.

Key engineering decisions

01

Transcribe on the device

Running Whisper in the browser keeps audio private and costs nothing per minute; the price is speed that depends on the learner’s hardware.

02

Validate model output like user input

Generated visual specs pass schema and semantic checks before rendering, with one repair round, so a bad generation fails safely instead of breaking the page.

03

Postgres in tests

PGlite runs the real migrations and policies in unit tests, so RLS is tested without a server.

Notes for reviewers

SecurityTwo migrations are dedicated to security fixes found in review; AI routes enforce per-guest and per-day limits.
Limits and next stepsTurn on payments, and move long AI jobs to a queue so the agent can run beyond a single request.
01

Problem statement

Students leave a class with a recording they rarely replay, slides, photographs of the board and a PDF chapter. Rereading feels like study but produces weak retention, and the supporting tools are split across separate applications for notes, flashcards and transcription, most of them in English only and dependent on uploading recordings to a server. French-speaking learners, in Cameroon in particular, are the least served.

02

Contribution

Mosaic converts each input into a note structured for study: the idea in plain words, an analogy, a roadmap, the explanation, a worked example, the key terms and the common errors. Lecture transcripts are divided into chapters whose timestamps replay the original moment. A retrieval sequence follows: Teach it back compares the learner’s own explanation with the key ideas and reports what is missing, then a quiz, spaced-repetition flashcards and a mock examination. Visualize turns a passage into an animated, interactive explanation, such as a parabola driven by sliders or a host obtaining its address through DHCP. A notebook with tags, tasks and calendar, a PDF viewer with highlights, a library and Mentor, an assistant whose proposed actions require confirmation, surround this core.

03

Architecture

Next.js 16 and React 19 in strict TypeScript, with Tailwind and next-intl providing complete English and French interfaces and TipTap as the editor. Notes and original files remain in the browser; accounts and synchronisation use Supabase Postgres with row-level security, and pdf.js renders documents. Card payments are implemented with Stripe Checkout and remain switched off.

04

Method and data

Whisper, compiled to WebAssembly, runs in a worker on the device; only the transcript and a few still frames are sent to Claude to draft the note. Claude also evaluates teach-back explanations and writes visual specifications, which are validated for structure and meaning before playback and returned once for repair if validation fails. Flashcard intervals are scheduled with FSRS.

05

Verification and limitations

536 unit and database tests and 210 end-to-end and accessibility tests (Playwright with axe) run against a production build on desktop and mobile profiles. Transcription speed depends on the learner’s hardware, and generated notes and visualisations, though validated for form, remain machine-written and should be checked against the source.
